home-energy-audit.title: Home energy audits in Winnipeg: EnerGuide evaluations, costs and rebates
home-energy-audit.description: Book an EnerGuide home energy audit in Winnipeg: 12 licensed organizations, local prices, Manitoba rebates and what 77% pre-1991 housing means for your upgrade list.
home-energy-audit.lede: 12 NRCan-licensed service organizations deliver EnerGuide home evaluations in Winnipeg. Here's what one costs, what it tends to find in Winnipeg houses, and which Manitoba rebates it unlocks.

sections.h2: What an evaluation finds in Winnipeg homes
sections.html:
Of Winnipeg's 202,915 houses (single-detached, semi-detached, row houses and duplexes), 37% were built before 1961 and 77% before 1991, according to the 2021 Census. The typical Winnipeg house dates from 1961–1970, and an evaluation is how you find out what that means for yours: the blower door measures air leakage, the advisor inspects the attic, walls, basement, windows and heating system, and the report ranks upgrades by what they'd save.

Winnipeg gets about 5,542 heating degree-days a year and has a winter design temperature of −31.3°C, according to NRCan's HOT2000 climate data for Winnipeg International. That's the 6th-highest heating demand of the 70 cities we cover. The more heating a climate needs, the more each fix is worth, which is why the evaluation's ranked list matters more in some cities than others.

In the Winnipeg area, 66% of households heat mainly with a forced-air furnace, 12% with electric baseboards and about 7% with a boiler and radiators; natural gas is the main heating energy for 56% of households and electricity for 27% (Statistics Canada, 2023). The heating system on the report shapes the recommendations: a forced-air furnace invites a ducted heat pump, electric baseboards a ductless one.

Efficiency Manitoba rebates $400 on a pre-retrofit EnerGuide evaluation if you own the home, it has Manitoba Hydro residential service and you plan at least one upgrade within 12 months. Apply within 90 days.

Most providers quote the initial (pre-upgrade) and follow-up (post-upgrade) visits separately. Rebate programs that pay on measured improvement need both, so ask for the combined price.

• Initial evaluation, about 2–3 hours. The advisor measures and inspects the house and runs the blower door test.
  • Report and EnerGuide rating. You get the home's energy rating in gigajoules per year and a list of recommended upgrades with estimated savings.
  • Do the work. Most rebate programs only count upgrades done after the initial evaluation.
  • Follow-up evaluation. A second visit measures the improvement, which is what most rebates pay on.

blower-door-test.title: Blower door test in Winnipeg: cost, who does it and why it matters here
blower-door-test.description: Where to get a blower door test in Winnipeg, what it costs, and why air leakage matters with 5,542 heating degree-days a year and 37% of houses built before 1961.
blower-door-test.lede: A blower door test measures how leaky a house is and shows where the leaks are. In Winnipeg, with about 5,542 heating degree-days a year, every leak runs up the heating bill for most of the year.

sections.h2: Why air leakage matters in Winnipeg
sections.html:
Winnipeg gets about 5,542 heating degree-days a year and has a winter design temperature of −31.3°C, according to NRCan's HOT2000 climate data for Winnipeg International. That's the 6th-highest heating demand of the 70 cities we cover.

Of Winnipeg's 202,915 houses (single-detached, semi-detached, row houses and duplexes), 37% were built before 1961 and 77% before 1991, according to the 2021 Census. Older houses usually test leakier than newer ones, and an EnerGuide report compares your result with homes of the same era, so you can see whether your house is typical or a problem.

• Combustion safety. In the Winnipeg area, the main heating energy is natural gas for 56% of households. A tighter house changes how fuel-burning appliances vent, so the spillage check should be repeated after serious air sealing. Combustion safety testing in Winnipeg
  • Radon. Sealing shifts the pressure balance between the house and the soil. Health Canada's 2012 survey found 12.1% of 66 homes tested in the Winnipeg Regional Health Authority health region above the guideline. The larger 2024 Cross-Canada survey reports 37.4% (1 in 3) of houses at or above the guideline for the Winnipeg, MB (Winnipeg CMA) metro area. Test before and after big air-sealing jobs. Radon testing in Winnipeg

A blower door test is part of every EnerGuide evaluation rather than a separate purchase. Efficiency Manitoba rebates $400 on a pre-retrofit EnerGuide evaluation if you own the home, it has Manitoba Hydro residential service and you plan at least one upgrade within 12 months. Apply within 90 days.

• A calibrated fan is fitted into an exterior door and pulls air out until the house is at 50 pascals, the standard test pressure.
  • The result is air changes per hour at 50 Pa (ACH50): how many times an hour the whole volume of air would leak out and be replaced at that pressure.
  • While the fan runs, you and the advisor walk the house and feel for leaks at the attic hatch, rim joists, pot lights, trim and plumbing and wiring penetrations.
  • A second test after the work shows what changed, and it is what most rebates pay on.

The blower door test in detail.

thermal-imaging.lede: An infrared camera shows missing insulation, air leaks and damp spots without opening a wall, but only when it's at least 10°C colder outside than inside. Winnipeg's long heating season gives you months of good scanning weather.

sections.html: Winnipeg gets about 5,542 heating degree-days a year and has a winter design temperature of −31.3°C, according to NRCan's HOT2000 climate data for Winnipeg International. That gives Winnipeg a long window, roughly late fall to early spring, when the inside-outside difference comfortably exceeds the 10°C an infrared scan needs.

Run it with the blower door test depressurizing the house and every leak shows up as a cold streak.

Most EnerGuide advisors include an infrared scan with the evaluation, but it isn't required, so confirm when you book. faq.q: Can a thermal camera see through walls?

heat-loss-calculation.title: Heat loss calculation in Winnipeg: sizing a heat pump for −31.3°C
heat-loss-calculation.description: A CSA F280 room-by-room heat loss calculation for Winnipeg homes, sized to the local −31.3°C design temperature: why it matters for heat pumps, what it costs and who does it.
heat-loss-calculation.lede: The heat loss calculation is how a heat pump or furnace gets sized for your house, and the key input is the design temperature: −31.3°C for Winnipeg, from NRCan's HOT2000 climate data for Winnipeg International.

sections.h2: Why the design temperature matters in Winnipeg
sections.html:
−31.3°C is the 5th-coldest design temperature of the 70 cities we cover. The F280 calculation works out how much heat each room loses on that design day, from the house's actual walls, windows, air leakage and ceiling insulation.

At −31.3°C, even cold-climate heat pumps lose capacity just when you need heat most. The room-by-room number tells you how much the heat pump can cover and how much backup heat to plan for, rather than guessing from square footage.

In the Winnipeg area, 66% of households heat mainly with a forced-air furnace, 12% with electric baseboards and about 7% with a boiler and radiators; natural gas is the main heating energy for 56% of households and electricity for 27% (Statistics Canada, 2023).

Contractors who size by square footage routinely oversize. An oversized heat pump costs more to buy, cycles on and off, dehumidifies poorly in summer and wears faster. An undersized one leans on backup heat. The F280 report is the evidence either way, and it's worth having before you compare quotes.

About $150–$400 as a standalone calculation (a September 2026 planning range; quotes vary). Many energy advisors bundle it with an EnerGuide evaluation, which also gives the calculation measured air-leakage data instead of an assumption.

providers.heading: NRCan-licensed service organizations serving Winnipeg
providers.note: Many energy advisors also do room-by-room CSA F280 calculations for an extra fee; HVAC designers do them too. Ask for the F280 report itself, not just an equipment recommendation.

ventilation-assessment.h1: Ventilation and humidity assessments in Winnipeg
ventilation-assessment.title: Ventilation and humidity assessment in Winnipeg: condensation, mold and HRVs
ventilation-assessment.description: Why Winnipeg homes get window condensation and musty air, what a ventilation and humidity assessment measures, and when an HRV or ERV makes sense. 17% of local houses were built since 2001.
ventilation-assessment.lede: Condensation on windows, musty basements and stuffy bedrooms are ventilation and humidity problems, and they're easy to confuse with insulation problems. A ventilation assessment measures which one you have.

sections.h2: Why Winnipeg homes get humidity problems
sections.html:
Winnipeg gets about 5,542 heating degree-days a year and has a winter design temperature of −31.3°C, according to NRCan's HOT2000 climate data for Winnipeg International. On Winnipeg's coldest days, window glass and poorly insulated corners get cold enough for condensation at humidity levels that feel normal indoors, so winter humidity needs to stay at the lower end of the comfortable range.

Of Winnipeg's 202,915 houses (single-detached, semi-detached, row houses and duplexes), 37% were built before 1961 and 77% before 1991, according to the 2021 Census. Newer houses (17% of Winnipeg's were built since 2001) are tight and usually have an HRV or ERV that needs balancing and cleaning. Older houses that get air-sealed can lose the accidental ventilation they used to rely on.

• Relative humidity in living areas and the basement.
  • Actual airflow from bath and kitchen fans, and whether they vent outside rather than into the attic.
  • How much fresh air the house gets, and whether an HRV or ERV is balanced.

The ventilation and humidity assessment in detail.

faq.q: HRV or ERV?
faq.a: Both bring in fresh air and recover heat. An ERV also transfers some moisture, which helps keep very dry winter air from getting drier; an HRV suits houses that tend to run humid.

faq.q: Why did condensation appear after we got new windows?
faq.a: Tighter windows cut accidental air leakage, so humidity builds up. The fix is usually controlled ventilation, not leakier windows.

attic-insulation-inspection.lede: The attic is usually the cheapest big energy fix in a house, and the inspection decides how to do it: how much insulation is there, where air leaks through the ceiling, and whether anything up there must not be disturbed.

sections.h2: What inspections find in Winnipeg attics
sections.html:
Of Winnipeg's 202,915 houses (single-detached, semi-detached, row houses and duplexes), 37% were built before 1961 and 77% before 1991, according to the 2021 Census. Attics in older houses commonly have a fraction of today's recommended insulation, and top-ups done over the years often buried air leaks instead of sealing them first.

Winnipeg gets about 5,542 heating degree-days a year and has a winter design temperature of −31.3°C, according to NRCan's HOT2000 climate data for Winnipeg International. That's the 6th-highest heating demand of the 70 cities we cover. The colder the climate, the faster added attic insulation pays for itself.

Vermiculite. Loose, pebbly, grey-brown or silver-gold insulation may contain asbestos. Health Canada's advice is not to disturb it; have it sampled before any attic work. Asbestos and vermiculite testing in Winnipeg

sections.h2: The right order for the work
sections.html:
• Seal the air leaks first: top plates, pot lights, plumbing stacks, the hatch.
  • Fix ventilation baffles so new insulation doesn't block soffit vents.
  • Then top up the insulation. Burying unsealed leaks under new insulation wastes much of the benefit.

What an attic inspection checks.

radon-testing.title: Radon testing in Winnipeg: local levels, test kits and certified professionals
radon-testing.description: Radon in Winnipeg: Health Canada survey results for the Winnipeg Regional Health Authority region (12.1% above the guideline), how to test for 3+ months, where to get kits and C-NRPP professionals locally.
radon-testing.lede: Radon is invisible, has no smell, and is the second-leading cause of lung cancer in Canada. In Health Canada's national survey, 12.1% of homes tested in the Winnipeg Regional Health Authority health region were above the guideline, and the only way to know about your house is to test it.

glance.sub: the Winnipeg, MB (Winnipeg CMA) metro area

sections.html:
Health Canada's 2012 survey found 12.1% of 66 homes tested in the Winnipeg Regional Health Authority health region above the guideline. The larger 2024 Cross-Canada survey reports 37.4% (1 in 3) of houses at or above the guideline for the Winnipeg, MB (Winnipeg CMA) metro area.

The two surveys aren't directly comparable: the 2024 study pooled about 69,000 volunteer tests and more of them were taken in basements, which partly explains its higher numbers. Neither can tell you about a single house, because neighbouring homes can differ widely.

• Use a long-term test of at least three months, with most of it in the heating season, which gives the most conservative result.
  • Place the detector in the lowest level you spend four or more hours a day in, away from drafts, and follow the kit's instructions.
  • If the result is above 200 Bq/m³, Health Canada recommends fixing it within a year, sooner if it's much higher.

Our full radon testing guide.

• The Manitoba Lung Association sells long-term kits and runs a library lending program, and Manitoba Hydro's Home Energy Efficiency Loan can finance radon mitigation up to $5,000 (C-NRPP-certified contractor required).
  • For a professional measurement or mitigation, search the C-NRPP directory by your Winnipeg postal code; it lists certified measurement and mitigation professionals.

• Manitoba's building code (the 2020 National Building Code) requires a soil-gas barrier and a radon rough-in in new homes.
  • The Canadian Lung Association's Lungs Matter program offers up to $1,500 toward mitigation for households with low to moderate incomes or a lung cancer diagnosis.
  • If your level is high, mitigation (usually a sub-slab depressurization fan system installed by a C-NRPP-certified professional) typically costs $2,000–$4,000.

faq.q: Is radon a problem in Winnipeg?
faq.a: Health Canada's 2012 survey found 12.1% of 66 homes tested in the Winnipeg Regional Health Authority health region above the guideline. The larger 2024 Cross-Canada survey reports 37.4% (1 in 3) of houses at or above the guideline for the Winnipeg, MB (Winnipeg CMA) metro area. Any home can have high radon, so Health Canada recommends testing every home.

faq.q: How long should a radon test take?
faq.a: At least three months, with most of it during the heating season. Short tests can't tell you your long-term average.

faq.q: Where can I get a radon test kit in Winnipeg?
faq.a: The Manitoba Lung Association sells long-term kits and runs a library lending program, and Manitoba Hydro's Home Energy Efficiency Loan can finance radon mitigation up to $5,000 (C-NRPP-certified contractor required). Hardware stores and lung associations also sell long-term kits for about $30–$60.

faq.q: What does radon mitigation cost?
faq.a: Typically $2,000–$4,000 for a sub-slab depressurization system installed by a C-NRPP-certified professional.

carbon-monoxide-testing.title: Carbon monoxide testing in Winnipeg: the Manitoba alarm rules and appliance checks
carbon-monoxide-testing.description: CO safety for Winnipeg homes: what Manitoba law requires, why it matters with 56% of households heating with natural gas, where alarms go and how appliances get checked.
carbon-monoxide-testing.lede: Carbon monoxide is odourless and can kill. Manitoba's Fire Code requires CO detection only in buildings subject to fire-safety inspections, not in ordinary private homes, so installing alarms is up to you.

sections.html: Manitoba's Fire Code requires CO detection only in buildings subject to fire-safety inspections, not in ordinary private homes, so installing alarms is up to you.

In the Winnipeg area, the main heating energy is natural gas for 56% of households (Statistics Canada, 2023). Any fuel-burning appliance, fireplace or attached garage is a potential CO source.

Single-detached houses make up 58% of Winnipeg's households; many have an attached garage, another reason to put an alarm near the door into the house.

• Alarms next to sleeping areas and on every storey, tested monthly and replaced by their end-of-life date (usually 7 to 10 years).
  • Annual service of fuel-burning appliances by a licensed technician.
  • A combustion spillage test during an energy evaluation, which catches a venting problem before it produces CO.

Our carbon monoxide guide · Combustion safety testing in Winnipeg

faq.q: Are carbon monoxide alarms mandatory in Winnipeg?
faq.a: Manitoba's Fire Code requires CO detection only in buildings subject to fire-safety inspections, not in ordinary private homes, so installing alarms is up to you.

faq.q: Where should CO alarms go?
faq.a: Outside every sleeping area and on every storey, following the manufacturer's instructions. Some rules also call for one near a fuel-burning appliance or the door from an attached garage.

faq.q: How long do CO alarms last?
faq.a: Most have an end-of-life date of 7 to 10 years printed on the unit; replace them by then even if they still beep when tested.

mold-testing.h1: Mold and air quality testing in Winnipeg
mold-testing.title: Mold testing in Winnipeg: air quality sampling and finding the moisture source
mold-testing.description: Mold and indoor air quality testing in Winnipeg: when sampling is worth $300–$600, why cold winters cause condensation, and how to find an accredited lab.
mold-testing.lede: Mold sampling tells you whether there's a hidden mold problem and roughly where. It doesn't tell you why, and fixing the moisture source is the actual cure.

sections.h2: Why mold shows up in Winnipeg homes
sections.html:
Winnipeg gets about 5,542 heating degree-days a year and has a winter design temperature of −31.3°C, according to NRCan's HOT2000 climate data for Winnipeg International. On cold days, exterior corners, closets on outside walls and window frames get cold enough for condensation, which is where mold usually starts in Winnipeg houses.

Of Winnipeg's 202,915 houses (single-detached, semi-detached, row houses and duplexes), 37% were built before 1961 and 77% before 1991, according to the 2021 Census. Older basements without a moisture barrier and houses that were air-sealed without adding ventilation are common trouble spots.

• You smell mustiness but can't find the source.
  • After a leak or flood, to check that cleanup worked.
  • Before buying an older house with signs of past water damage.

If you can see mould, you usually don't need a test to know it's there; you need to fix the moisture and clean it up properly.

No Canadian province has a mandatory mould standard for homes. Health Canada's guideline sets no numerical limit: it says to fix moisture problems and clean up visible mould.

Ask any Winnipeg tester which lab analyzes their samples, and look for one accredited under AIHA's EMLAP program for environmental microbiology. Pair sampling with a ventilation and humidity assessment, which finds the cause.

Ventilation and humidity assessments in Winnipeg · Our mold and indoor air quality guide

faq.q: How much does mold testing cost in Winnipeg?
faq.a: Plan on about $300–$600 for a typical sampling visit (a September 2026 planning range); lab fees for extra samples add to that.

faq.q: Do I need a test if I can see mould?
faq.a: Usually not. Visible mould needs cleanup and a fix for the moisture source. Testing helps most when you suspect mould you can't see.

faq.q: Is there a legal mould limit for homes in Canada?
faq.a: No. Health Canada sets no numerical limit; its guidance is to control moisture and clean up mould. Quebec has a voluntary handling standard.

asbestos-testing.h1: Asbestos and vermiculite testing in Winnipeg
asbestos-testing.title: Asbestos testing in Winnipeg: vermiculite, labs and the Manitoba rules
asbestos-testing.description: Asbestos and vermiculite testing in Winnipeg, where 77% of houses were built before 1991: what to sample, lab costs and the Manitoba rules for renovation.
asbestos-testing.lede: About 156,200 Winnipeg houses (77%) were built before 1991, when asbestos still turned up in insulation, flooring, plaster and duct wrap. A lab test before renovation is the only way to know.

sections.h2: Where asbestos shows up in Winnipeg houses
sections.html:
Of Winnipeg's 202,915 houses (single-detached, semi-detached, row houses and duplexes), 37% were built before 1961 and 77% before 1991, according to the 2021 Census.

  • Vermiculite attic insulation: loose, pebbly, grey-brown or silver-gold granules.
  • Vinyl floor tiles and their adhesive, textured ceilings and some plaster.
  • Duct wrap and pipe insulation on older heating systems.

Manitoba's workplace rules treat suspect material as asbestos until a qualified person says otherwise, and from June 1, 2027, asbestos sampling and abatement work will require a provincial certificate.

Whatever the rules, don't sand, cut or remove suspect material yourself before it's tested.

A trained assessor takes small samples, and an accredited lab analyzes them; plan on about $50–$150 per sample. Asbestos labs in Canada are typically accredited under NIST's NVLAP program.

Our asbestos and vermiculite guide · Attic inspections in Winnipeg

faq.q: Do I need an asbestos test before renovating in Winnipeg?
faq.a: If the house was built before 1991 and the work will disturb insulation, flooring, plaster or duct wrap, test first. Manitoba's workplace rules treat suspect material as asbestos until a qualified person says otherwise, and from June 1, 2027, asbestos sampling and abatement work will require a provincial certificate.

faq.q: How much does asbestos testing cost?
faq.a: About $50–$150 per lab sample, plus the assessor's visit. Abatement, if needed, is quoted separately.

faq.q: What should I do if I have vermiculite in the attic?
faq.a: Leave it alone, keep the attic closed, and have it sampled before any attic work. Health Canada advises against disturbing it or removing it yourself.

lead-paint-testing.title: Lead paint testing in Winnipeg: which homes are at risk and how to test
lead-paint-testing.description: 37% of Winnipeg's houses were built before 1961, when lead paint was common. How to test with $15–$40 swabs or a lab, and how to renovate safely.
lead-paint-testing.lede: Health Canada says a home built before 1960 probably has lead paint somewhere. That's 37% of Winnipeg's houses (built before 1961, per the 2021 Census), plus exterior paint on many of the 40% built from 1961 to 1990.

sections.h2: Which Winnipeg homes are at risk
sections.html:
Of Winnipeg's 202,915 houses (single-detached, semi-detached, row houses and duplexes), 37% were built before 1961 and 77% before 1991, according to the 2021 Census.

  • Built before 1960: probably has lead-based paint (Health Canada).
  • Built 1960–1990: exterior paint may contain lead, and interior paint may contain smaller amounts.
  • Built after 1990: consumer paints were virtually lead-free by then.

• Swab kits ($15–$40) give a quick screen of the surfaces you plan to disturb.
  • For certainty, send paint chips to a lab accredited under AIHA's ELLAP program, or hire a firm with an X-ray fluorescence (XRF) analyzer.
  • Test before sanding, stripping or replacing old windows and trim.

Our lead paint guide.

Don't dry-sand, use a heat gun or power-wash it. Contain the work area, mist surfaces, clean with a HEPA vacuum, and keep children and pregnant people away until cleanup is done. No province has a lead-paint rule aimed at homeowners, but contractors in B.C. and Yukon must include lead in pre-renovation or demolition hazard inspections.

faq.q: Does my Winnipeg house have lead paint?
faq.a: If it was built before 1960, probably; 1960–1990, possibly on the exterior. Test the surfaces you plan to disturb.

faq.q: Are lead test swabs reliable?
faq.a: They are a useful screen. For renovation decisions, confirm with a lab analysis of paint chips or an XRF reading.

faq.q: What does lead paint testing cost?
faq.a: Swab kits run about $15–$40; lab analysis and XRF testing cost more and are quoted by the firm.

well-water-testing.title: Well water testing in Winnipeg: how to test and what it costs in Manitoba
well-water-testing.description: Private well water testing in Winnipeg: most homes are on city water, but some rely on wells. How Manitoba's testing program works, what it costs and how often to test.
well-water-testing.lede: Winnipeg homes are served by the City's municipal water system, so private drinking-water wells are rare. If yours is, here's how testing works in Manitoba.

sections.html:
Winnipeg homes are served by the City's municipal water system, so private drinking-water wells are rare.

Local program: Manitoba's subsidized once-a-year well bacteria test ($17.67) is done at Duracan Laboratory, 862 Dufferin Ave., Winnipeg. Details

Manitoba's Private Well Testing Subsidy covers one bacteria test a year for $17.67 at Duracan Laboratory in Winnipeg, with a free re-test after a positive result. Test at least once a year, ideally after snowmelt.

• Bacteria (total coliforms and E. coli): at least once a year, and after flooding, heavy rain or work on the well.
  • Nitrate, especially near farmland or septic systems.
  • Metals and naturally occurring contaminants such as arsenic, uranium or manganese when a well is new and every few years after, depending on local geology.

Our well water guide.

faq.q: Is well water testing free in Manitoba?
faq.a: Manitoba's Private Well Testing Subsidy covers one bacteria test a year for $17.67 at Duracan Laboratory in Winnipeg, with a free re-test after a positive result. Test at least once a year, ideally after snowmelt.

faq.q: How often should I test my well?
faq.a: For bacteria, at least once a year and after flooding, heavy rain or well work; many health units recommend more often. Test chemistry when the well is new and every few years after.

faq.q: Are private wells common in Winnipeg?
faq.a: Winnipeg homes are served by the City's municipal water system, so private drinking-water wells are rare.

commercial-energy-audit.title: Commercial energy audits in Winnipeg: reporting rules and incentives
commercial-energy-audit.description: Commercial and multi-unit building energy audits in Winnipeg: ASHRAE levels, no mandatory reporting rule, and 2 utility or government incentives for audits and studies.
commercial-energy-audit.lede: Offices, apartment buildings, retail and industrial sites get engineering energy audits rather than EnerGuide evaluations. Here's what applies in Winnipeg: no mandatory reporting rule and 2 incentive programs we found for audits and studies.

sections.h2: Reporting rules that apply in Winnipeg
sections.html: • Building Energy Disclosure Project (BEDP) (voluntary): Voluntary and free, started 2020. Eligible: commercial or institutional buildings in Winnipeg of at least 20,000 sq ft that are at least 70% occupied. No mandatory by-law found. Source

• Commercial Energy Audit Program (Efficiency Manitoba): Up to 50% of the cost of an ASHRAE Level 2 or Level 3 audit by a pre-qualified consultant. Caps (L2 / L3): office, education, hotel, recreation/arena, healthcare, multi-unit residential or industrial-with-offices buildings of 4+ storeys (any size) or 1-3 storeys over 60,000 sq ft: $3,200 / $12,500; 1-3 storeys 30,000-60,000 sq ft: $2,200 / $8,000; 1-3 storeys under 30,000 sq ft, and all other building types: $1,200 / $4,200. Details
  • Small Business Program (Efficiency Manitoba): Free installation of basic energy-saving products plus a free lighting and pitched-roof attic insulation assessment to see if a Premium Upgrade fits. Details

• Level 1, walk-through: a site visit and bill review that benchmarks the building and lists low-cost measures.
  • Level 2, energy survey and analysis: where the energy goes, with savings and cost estimates per measure. Most incentive applications use this level.
  • Level 3, detailed analysis: monitoring and modelling for capital-intensive projects.

Ask which level a quote covers. Audits are done by engineering firms and energy consultants; look for a P.Eng. and credentials such as the Certified Energy Manager (CEM). How commercial energy audits work.

faq.q: Do Winnipeg buildings have to report energy use?
faq.a: We found no mandatory reporting rule for Winnipeg buildings as of September 28, 2026.

faq.q: Are there incentives for commercial energy audits in Winnipeg?
faq.a: Yes: Commercial Energy Audit Program; Small Business Program. Check eligibility and pre-approval rules before you commission the audit.

faq.q: What does a commercial energy audit cost?
faq.a: It depends on the building's size and the ASHRAE level. Get quotes that state the level and the deliverables.
